original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-abelian}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. The category
$\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is an abelian category. Moreover
a complex
$$
\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H}
$$
is exact at $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if for all $x \in X$ the
complex
$$
\mathcal{F}_x \to \mathcal{G}_x \to \mathcal{H}_x
$$
is exact at $\mathcal{G}_x$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$f_* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is left exact. In fact it commutes with all limits.
\item The functor
$f^* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
is right exact. In fact it commutes with all colimits.
\item Pullback $f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$
on abelian sheaves is exact.
\end{enumerate}

\item The functor

is right exact. In fact it commutes with all colimits.
\item Pullback $f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$

\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
conclusions:
The functor
$f_* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is left exact. In fact it commutes with all limits.

The functor
$f^* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
is right exact. In fact it commutes with all colimits.

Pullback $f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$
on abelian sheaves is exact.

semantic_review_note: For a morphism of ringed spaces, pushforward of modules preserves all limits and is left exact; module pullback preserves all colimits and is right exact; inverse image of abelian sheaves is exact. All three enumerated source clauses and categories are retained.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-j-shriek-exact}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of topological spaces.
The functor $j_! : \textit{Ab}(U) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$
is exact.

final_content.statement:
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of topological spaces.
The functor $j_! : \textit{Ab}(U) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$
is exact.
hypotheses: Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of topological spaces.

semantic_review_note: For an open embedding of topological spaces j:U→X, extension by zero j_! on sheaves of abelian groups is exact. The source concerns abelian sheaves, not merely presheaves or modules.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-section-direct-sum-quasi-compact}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $I$ be a set. For $i \in I$, let $\mathcal{F}_i$
be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
For $U \subset X$ quasi-compact open the map
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_i(U)
\longrightarrow
\left(\bigoplus\nolimits_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_i\right)(U)
$$
is bijective.
hold_reason: The pinned theorem universally quantifies a family (F_i)_{i∈I} of O_X-module sheaves before asserting sections commute with the direct sum on every quasi-compact open U. The proposed hypotheses stop at 'I is a set'; the family and its sheaf type are embedded in the conclusions, so the structured hypothesis/result split fails to carry the universal family quantifier and its scope.
proposed_correction: Move 'For each i∈I let F_i be an O_X-module sheaf' and U quasi-compact into hypotheses; keep bijectivity of ⊕ F_i(U)→(⊕F_i)(U) as conclusion; new independent check.
